name: home-at-last
description: FAMOUS DRUM SOUND #3: Steely Dan 'Home at Last' (Aja, 1977 / the Bernard Purdie half-time shuffle). The CLEAN / hi-fi THIRD axis — vs the room-dominant warm-dark Bonham 'fool-in-the-rain' and the crushed/dark/mono Beatles 'tomorrow-never-knows': warm-but-DETAILED, DYNAMIC with the snare ghost-note dynamics PRESERVED (crest held/up — never crushed, never breathing-glue), TIGHT/ROUND controlled low end, SILKY EXTENDED top (no harshness, no roll-off-to-dark), and NATURAL balanced width (not mono, not wide-room). Anchored on Pultec EQP-1A passive program EQ (low-end trick + air-without-fizz) -> Manley Variable Mu vari-mu tube glue in COMP/slow-attack (levels macro-dynamics, KEEPS transients) -> Studer A800 30 IPS tape (controlled warmth, the INVERSE of Bonham's 15 IPS bloom). This is the studio TONE, not Purdie's performed shuffle GROOVE, and unlike Bonham it does NOT need room mics (Aja was close-mic'd). Dev-validated 2026-06-03 on a 45 s artifacts/drums clip (a bright, HYPER-dynamic, non-Aja stress kit). Honest era PROXY chain — NOT a claim of the literal Aja signal path (see notes).
pipeline: 1. SOURCE: phase-aligned multi-mic stems (close mics: kick + snare + hi-hat + toms + overheads). Room mics OPTIONAL and MINIMAL — Aja used NONE (close-mic'd kit); a room channel, if present, is used only for tasteful depth, far down. (The OPPOSITE of fool-in-the-rain, which requires room mics.)

2. PER-STEM PROCESS: scripts/mix/process_stems.py with presets/mix/home-at-last-stem-process.plans.json (declick OFF; CLEAN + DETAILED + dynamics-preserving: gentle de-box, gentle de-harsh, a TOUCH of clean top detail/air ALLOWED — the only famous-drum recipe that does — but NO gating and NO transient snap, and LOW comp ratios, so the loud-backbeat/quiet-ghost-note contrast survives) -> <kit>/processed-hal/.

3. CLEAN balance: scripts/mix/balance_stems.py with the per-role targets below (measured LUFS; snare/kit-FORWARD, present detailed hat, kick tight & supportive, OH clean image, room minimal) -> bus_hal_pre.wav.

4. HOME-AT-LAST BUS: scripts/mix/home_at_last_bus.py bus_hal_pre.wav bus_hal.wav (Pultec EQP-1A -> Manley Variable Mu -> Studer 30 IPS tape -> gentle zero-phase polish -> natural width; params in that script).

balance_targets_lufs._method: measured integrated LUFS per stem, gained to target; one global -6 dBFS-peak headroom trim on the sum (NOT peak-normalized per stem). The CLEAN/BALANCED studio mix: the snare (the shuffle's ghost-note star) is FORWARD, the kick tight & supportive, the hat present + detailed, the overheads carry a clean kit image, and the room (if any) is MINIMAL. Neither room-forward (Bonham) nor tom/close-forward-dark (TNK).

snare top._note: THE STAR — the Purdie ghost-note shuffle; full round body, NOT gated (ghost-note dynamics survive)

kick in._note: tight, round, deep, controlled — supportive, not boomy

hi hat._note: PRESENT + smooth + detailed (the triplet shuffle hat is a defining element — louder than Bonham's barely-there hat)

snare bottom._note: a clean touch of wires / ghost-note snap under the top

drum room._note: OPTIONAL — tasteful, CONTROLLED depth only (Aja used NO room mics); omit it for the most authentic close-mic Aja sound

bus_chain._impl: scripts/mix/home_at_last_bus.py — authoritative; a bare invocation reproduces these. Pultec/Manley/Studer are driven inline via Pedalboard set_param (nearest-valid snap), the same mechanism as the preset harness; apply-vst-chain's float dict would drop the string enums (Pultec low_freq/high_freq/hf_atten_freq/enable/output; Manley recovery/comp_lim/hp_sc_filt/matrices/links).
1_eq_pre_zero_phase: high_pass 30 Hz q0.707 (gentle subsonic; KEEP the round low end)

2_pultec_eqp_1a._intent: the Aja tonal signature via passive tube/transformer EQ (colour is the CURVES, not drive — ~0.01% THD). LOW-END TRICK: boost+atten @60 CPS = a big-but-TIGHT round bottom with a low-mid scoop (no mud). AIR-WITHOUT-FIZZ: 16 KCS broad boost (hf_q 8 = BROAD/musical) + an independent 5 KCS atten = silky extended top while the 3-8 kHz harsh/fizz is shaved. dial knobs are 0-10 POSITIONS, nonlinear, NOT dB.

3_manley_variable_mu._intent: CLEAN vari-mu tube glue that LEVELS macro-dynamics while KEEPING transients — crest HOLDS/RISES (the measured no-tape variant rose 30.8->27.8). COMP (1.5:1), slow attack (3 = let the ghost-note + backbeat transients through), Med recovery (most open), HP-SC In (the kick doesn't pump the bus). threshold maps DIRECTLY (lower = more GR; 5 = gentle). MUST stay in COMP not LIMIT — the Purdie shuffle IS its dynamics; if crest collapses you over-compressed -> raise l/r_thresh.

4_studer_a800_tape._intent: Clean, warm tape glue with a CONTROLLED bottom. 30 IPS NOT 15: the head-bump sits UP at ~100-120 Hz (upper-bass body) instead of 15 IPS's deeper ~50-60 Hz sub-BLOOM (the fool-in-the-rain move) = a tighter, more controlled low end (the repo's warm-tight default; do NOT 'fix' to 15). NOTE: by spectral centroid this A800 model measures 30 IPS slightly DARKER than 15 (it darkens overall AND adds the ~100 Hz weight — see docs/vst/studer-a800.md), so the DETAILED top is kept by repro_hf_eq 5.0 (higher than the warm recipes' 2.0; NOT TNK's 1.5 darkening), NOT by the IPS alone. input_level 1.5 = GENTLE drive (warmth/glue without grit; Aja is clean). Historically apt: Aja was tracked to a 2" Stephens machine at 30 IPS non-Dolby.

5_eq_post_zero_phase: low_shelf 100 +0.5 dB q0.7 (subtle weight; the Pultec did the bulk)
bell 400 -1.0 dB q1.0 (gentle de-box; keep it clean)
bell 3000 -1.0 dB q1.2 (smoothness guard; Aja is never harsh)
high_shelf 12000 +0.5 dB q0.7 (clean sheen/detail, NOT bright)

6_stereo_width._intent: NATURAL width — default 1.0 is a NO-OP (the stage is skipped). Aja is a balanced studio image: do NOT narrow toward mono (that's TNK) and do NOT hyper-widen (that's a room sound). Tunable via --width if a source needs it.

bus_chain.7_output: peak-normalize to -1 dBFS (mix bus — NOT mastered)

approved_signature_full_kit._measured_on: a 45 s clip of the artifacts/drums kit — a BRIGHT (pre-bus centroid 5085), HYPER-dynamic (pre-bus crest 30.8), narrow (pre-bus corr 0.922) NON-Aja stress kit. Pre-bus (clean snare/kit-forward balance): centroid 5085 / tilt -1.21 / crest 30.8 / corr 0.922 / LUFS -29.3. LOCKED 2026-06-03: the bare DEFAULTS won the .claude/workflows/home-at-last.js Gemini judge panel (34/50) over 6 variants, and a SEQUENTIAL re-render reproduced these meters exactly (deterministic; an independent re-measure of the locked file agreed: TP -0.99 dBTP).
approved_signature_full_kit._judge_panel: /home-at-last 5-lens Gemini panel — winner default_30ips 34/50: clean 8, dynamics 9, top 9, low 5, width 3. The two LOW lens scores are SOURCE artifacts of this narrow/hyper-dynamic stress kit, NOT chain defects: 'width 3 / effectively mono' is the kit itself (pre-bus corr 0.922; the recipe's width=1.0 PRESERVES the source image — on a real Aja kit with wide overheads this scores high), and 'low 5 / boxy ~300-400 Hz' cites a -6.11 dB/oct tilt that is Gemini's MONO-DOWNMIX artifact (the pure-DSP tilt is -2.16). Runner-up airier_top (--pul-hf-boost 6 --pul-hf-atten 1, +16k air) ALSO 34/50 (centroid 5399) — a valid 'more open top' alternative. Rejected directions: bloom_15ips 27 (15 IPS is the Bonham move, not Aja), more_glue 29 / most_dynamic 25 (the Manley HOLDS crest ~25.9 even pushed — its signature), bigger_low 23 (a harder low-end trick over-darkened: tilt -2.44, crest 24.3 — keep the Pultec at B5/A4).
approved_signature_full_kit._what_to_check: the DIRECTION, not absolutes: (1) crest stays HIGH = DYNAMICS PRESERVED (the signature trait). 30.8->25.9 here is GENTLE leveling of an extreme source; isolation proves the Manley HOLDS crest (no-tape variant 30.8->27.8, ~= the Bonham bus's 28.0) and the 30 IPS tape costs the last ~2 dB for the warm tight bottom (no-Manley 25.6) — both FAR above a crushed bus (TNK ~17). On a controlled Aja-like source expect crest to barely move. (2) centroid HELD (5085->4856, only ~-230) = the top DETAIL is kept (NOT Bonham's ~-1000 darkening, NOT TNK's hard roll-off). (3) tilt gently WARM (-1.21->-2.16), not dark. (4) correlation NATURAL (~0.96) = a clean centered studio image, NOT mono (TNK ~0.99) and NOT a wide room (Bonham ~0.80); the ABSOLUTE value tracks the SOURCE width (this stress kit is narrow at 0.922).

notes: This is the studio TONE (clean/hi-fi, warm-but-detailed, DYNAMIC, tight-round low, silky top, natural width), NOT Bernard Purdie's performed half-time shuffle GROOVE — the groove + ghost-note placement live in the source performance. The chain merely PRESERVES the dynamic range that keeps the whisper-quiet ghost notes audible against the full-volume backbeat.

DYNAMICS ARE THE POINT. Keep the Manley in COMP (not LIMIT) with a slow attack + HP sidechain so crest HOLDS/RISES; no gating, no transient snap, low per-stem comp ratios. If crest collapses you erased the ghost-note contrast — back the threshold off.
Does NOT need room mics (the OPPOSITE of fool-in-the-rain): Aja was close-mic'd with no room mics; a room channel, if present, is used minimally for depth (omit it for the most authentic Aja sound).
Warmth = Pultec passive EQ + Studer 30 IPS tape + a gentle tilt, NEVER an aggressive bright boost. The top is silky/extended via air-WITHOUT-fizz (the 3-8 kHz harshness is SHAVED, not pushed).

30 IPS, not 15 — gives a FLATTER / more CONTROLLED low end (the head-bump moves up out of the musical bottom), the inverse of the 15 IPS bloom that makes fool-in-the-rain big. Do NOT 'fix' it to 15 (some find 15 subjectively fuller — that's the Bonham move, not this one).

HONEST NUANCE (the real recording): Aja (rel. 1977-09-23), produced by Gary Katz; 'Home at Last' is a Bernard Purdie session. The album won the 1978 Grammy for Best Engineered Recording (Non-Classical), shared by Roger Nichols (credited executive engineer), Bill Schnee, Elliot Scheiner, and Al Schmitt — do NOT attribute a single per-track engineer (the popular 'Schnee only did Aja/Black Cow' split is refuted; the real picture is a tracking-vs-overdubs split). Core tracking was at Producers' Workshop (Hollywood Blvd) to a 2" 24-track Stephens machine at 30 IPS non-Dolby, through a home-made console with Langevin AM16 preamps + a passive Langevin EQ251 (NOT a Pultec); overdubs at The Village Recorder; mixed via a Quad 8 at Sound Labs. The documented kit capture (close mics only, NO room mics, NO compression on the drums, 'a little EQ') is from the Steve Gadd TITLE-TRACK session — 'Home at Last' (Purdie) has no comparable documentation, so don't over-claim the exact path.

HONEST PROXY: Pultec EQP-1A + Manley Variable Mu + Studer A800 30 IPS is an era-appropriate chase of the clean/warm/DYNAMIC tone, NOT a claim of Aja's actual gear (the room used a passive Langevin EQ, not a Pultec, and there is no documented drum bus compressor / vari-mu on the kit). Run .claude/workflows/home-at-last.js to A/B Pultec/Manley/tape amounts and lock the winner's meters.
Wendel (Roger Nichols' drum sampler) was NOT on Aja — it's a Gaucho-era (1980) invention; a common confusion when discussing Aja drums.
This is a MIX bus (peak -1, NOT mastered) — hand to master-track for loudness/limiting and loops-to-deliverables for loops.
